items.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011
items.q: I remember one book, Bugs Bower or something, with little phrases and things, and I bought that book and I looked through that thing

ctx.x: Well I didn’t know a lot. And I watched you and Carmen and Dolores, and especially you and Carmen, like how you handled that gig. So I’m a bit curious like how did you know that? Because we’re almost the same age, but I had no idea at the time. How did you learn how to play that gig?

Well by that point I had played a lot of gigs for a lot of years, since I was 13 years old. And they were essentially the same kind of gig, one variation — aside from a few years with rock groups and, you know, on the road with some crazy bands. But most of the gigs were that kind of dance music, jazz, you know, not a full out blowing gig but, you know. So there was a lot of years there. And yeah, that information was not necessarily from that fake book either, I don’t mean to imply by that fake book like that…
I can recall people coming up and requesting a song, “Flamingo” or even something that might have been on the radio at the time like “Spanish Eyes” or something.
